headline: Serial-section registration and multimodal models extend spatial omics toward volumetric tissue maps
label: 3D Spatial Omics Reconstruction
summary: THiRST rebuilds 3D transcriptomics from serial sections while CORAL, DIRAC and GeneSPOT advance multiscale integration and spatial gene dynamics across conditions and time.
synthesis: Only THiRST among the current items directly reconstructs 3D spatial transcriptomics, using morphology-guided registration of serial 2D sections to build multi-resolution volumes. The remaining items mostly extend spatial omics analysis in other directions. CORAL and DIRAC integrate multimodal and cross-study spatial data, with DIRAC adding label transfer. GeneSPOT applies gene-centric optimal transport to quantify reorganization of spatial gene relationships across conditions and time. MorphoANOVA links H&E morphology to gene expression, SSAF-T infers cell types without segmentation, and Sphinx models adaptive neighborhoods in spatial proteomics. Compared with the earlier emphasis on reference-free generative reconstruction, the current evidence centers on registration-based volumes and on integration and statistical frameworks. Histology serves as a recurring anchor.
